meep_fem_prediction.reduced_because: meep_check() ran as a light job under a self-chosen 1.5 GB cap and was killed at 1.52 GB; its FEM mesh was then coarsened from scale 0.7071 to 1.0 and the job re-run under 2.5 GB (peak 2.37 GB, before the gc fix; the Meep subprocess counts in the RSS)
meep_fem_prediction.accuracy_cost_basis: the strip's n_eff_bent changes by 1.6e-5 from 15 to 10 nm (modes_strip400x200 convergence); lambda * dn / n_g = 1307.5 nm * 1.6e-5 / 4.14 = 0.005 nm, against the +-0.23 nm Meep uncertainty; the exact - isotropic difference is taken on one mesh, so the bias largely cancels in it
meep_fem_prediction.fits: 0.7071 adds ~31k dofs (~0.2 GB): fits the 3 GB light default and the 6 GB heavy cap

validation.conclusion: the exact (anisotropic) transform is right: it reproduces the analytic Bessel eigenvalue of a 2-D ring to < 1e-7 for both polarizations, Tidy3D's +/-R mean bend shift in 3-D to within 2 % at r_ref and 7.5 um (three cross-sections), and the cylindrical Meep resonance within the extrapolation range. femwell's isotropic eps(1+x/R)^2 overestimates the bend shift (x3.7 at R = 7.5 um; the excess scales as 1/R^2), because it approximates the conformal coordinate ln(r/R) by x/R and drops the mu tensor. modes.py uses the exact transform.

meep_order_sensitivity.note: free-order Richardson on every consecutive triple of the averaged series; the half-range of their limits is comparable to the 2.04 nm exact-isotropic difference, so the Meep check alone only disfavours the isotropic map (it needs an order outside the observed range); the decisive checks are the analytic Bessel benchmark and the Tidy3D bend shifts
